question: A sum of ₹10,00,000 amounts to ₹10,92,727 in 3 years at a certain rate of interest per annum, compounded annually. The rate of interest per annum is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For Compound Interest, multiplying factor = t√(Amount ÷ Principal).

Here, Time (t) = 3 years, so we find the cube root of the ratio.

⇒ ³√(1092727 ÷ 1000000) = 103 ÷ 100

This means ₹100 becomes ₹103 in 1 year.

Rate of interest = (103 − 100) ÷ 100 × 100% = 3%.

**∴ The correct answer is 3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Principal (P)
 ₹10,00,000
 
 Amount (A)
 ₹10,92,727
 

 

 Time = 3 Years
 Rate = R%

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹10,00,000

Amount (A) = ₹10,92,727

Time (t) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)t

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1092727 = 1000000 × (1 + R ÷ 100)³

⇒ 1092727 ÷ 1000000 = (1 + R ÷ 100)³

⇒ (103 ÷ 100)³ = (1 + R ÷ 100)³

Taking cube root on both sides:

⇒ 103 ÷ 100 = 1 + R ÷ 100

⇒ R ÷ 100 = 103 ÷ 100 − 1

⇒ R ÷ 100 = (103 − 100) ÷ 100

⇒ R ÷ 100 = 3 ÷ 100

⇒ R = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate Method

For 2 years, the effective CI rate = R + R + (R×R)÷100 %. This is faster for calculating exact compound interest when rates are small numbers.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years: Difference = P × (R÷100)².
For 3 years: Difference = P × (R÷100)² × (3 + R÷100).

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R÷2) and the given time period is doubled (2t) before applying the formula.
